Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
115 PM EDT Thu Oct 8 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 311 AM EDT Thursday...

No significant changes.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 311 AM EDT Thursday...

1. Unsettled pattern prevails through Friday with several 
rounds of showers expected, with greatest concentration over the
higher terrain.

2. Cooler and drier weather develops late Friday into Saturday,
with patchy frost possible in the Champlain Valley on Saturday 
morning. 

3. Remnants of tropical system to bring rain to parts of our 
region.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 311 AM EDT Thursday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: An upper level low slowly builds into the region
today and tomorrow, bringing several rounds of showers as 
shortwaves pivot around the longwave trough. Instability will 
reach its maximum today and some of the stronger showers will 
likely contain thunder. Pea sized hail will be possible, and 
maybe graupel in the higher terrain. The highest chances for 
showers will be farther north where the better dynamics and 
coldest air aloft will be. A lowering inversion heading into 
Friday should prevent any thunder chances, with instability only
reaching up to around 10,000 feet and not significantly 
surpassing -10 Celsius. However, the airmass will continue to 
cool and temperatures at the summits are expected to fall below 
freezing on Friday, so a few flurries/snow showers will be 
possible in the mountains, especially farther north. Snow levels
look to drop to around 3,500-4,000 feet. Flow remains unblocked
heading through Friday as the inversion will stay well above 
summit level.

KEY MESSAGE 2: Surface high pressure builds in for the weekend,
leading to a couple classic fall days. Highs will be in the 50s
and 60s with mostly sunny skies. Radiational cooling conditions
will become somewhat favorable for Friday night, but some 
lingering boundary flow may prevent the most efficient 
temperature decreases. The boundary layer looks to decouple at 
least in the later part of the night though. Frost formation is 
expected across most of the region, but it looks more uncertain 
in the Champlain Valley, the only area left in the growing 
season. Temperatures there will be marginal and winds there will
likely hold on the longest.

KEY MESSAGE 3: The remnants of Isaias will bring some rain to 
southern portions of our forecast area Sunday night into Monday.
Not expecting any strong winds with this system. Northern 
extent of precipitation is uncertain. For now have highest 
chances for precipitation from Saranac Lake NY to Montpelier VT 
and areas south of there.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z THURSDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...
Through 18Z Friday...Shower activity has been a bit more
widespread than initially forecast but the impacts have been
very minor. With plenty of drier air in the low levels, we have
seen some light rain and many terminals but no decrease in
visibility. This trend will continue through 00Z with scattered
showers briefly impacting terminals with no impact to flight
categories. Winds will remain gusty out of the west this
afternoon with gusts up to 25-30 knots at times. Some of the
showers have produced stronger gusts in excess of 30 knots but
these increases have been very short-lived. Winds will drop
below 10 knots after 00Z with light westerly winds continuing
overnight. Winds will once again become gusty after 12Z on
Friday in the 15 to 20 knot range at all terminals. VFR ceilings
and visibilities will continue through the TAF period.

Outlook...

Friday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Saturday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Saturday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Sunday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Sunday Night: Mainly VFR, with local IFR possible. Chance SHRA.
Columbus Day: Mainly MVFR, with areas IFR possible. Slight chance
SHRA.
Monday Night: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Chance SHRA.
Tuesday: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Likely SHRA.

&&
